reason: Bridge to Reasoning. reasoning_so_that asserts that CISA, FDA, NHTSA and ENISA publish joint disclosure-and-remediation guidance, and the newest bridge is a direct observation of the opposite: validation.4d1ed88cbce397cd (2026-07-28, relevance 4, dim=so_that) records two AI-found or AI-assisted flaws surfacing on the same day into 'entirely different disclosure regimes, with nothing connecting them' - HAWK producing a standardisation problem with no identifier at all, CVE-2026-53264 carrying a CVSS 7.8 and backports to seven stable lines but 'no KEV entry, no cross-sector advisory, and public exploit code'. That is the prediction's own stated bear case (parallel-but-unreconciled sectoral responses) showing up as the observed default, and the four-clause reasoning bundle carries no hedge for it. Separately, reasoning_given rests on three forcing functions - EU CRA 2027 in-force, the FDA 2027 refresh, the CISA Secure by Design pledge - and across the only three bridges this prediction has ever received (2026-06-01, 2026-06-06, 2026-07-28) nothing touches the pledge programme or the FDA refresh; the one institutional datapoint, the June 6 executive order's AI Cybersecurity Clearinghouse, is a different vehicle than the one reasoning_landing names ('four-authority MoU or joint advisory'). Reframe given and landing to the mechanism the evidence actually shows moving.
